practiceNotes: This is a proposed prerequisite graph, not certification of mastery or authorization to perform regulated work.

Use spaced retrieval for definitions, assumptions, representations, mechanism distinctions and method selection. Assess proof writing, implementation, experimental technique and extended modeling separately.
Require delayed transfer tasks, not only repeated familiar exercises; retain error analyses, code tests, laboratory notebooks and model-validation reports as performance evidence.

Chemical, biological, radiation, laser and electrical experiments require appropriate facilities, training, supervision and local authorization. Simulations and archived data can support, but do not certify, physical laboratory skill.
Human-participant, animal, ecological collection and genetically modified organism work requires applicable ethics review, permits, containment and welfare procedures.
Security exercises must use isolated, authorized systems and synthetic or consented data. Distributed fault experiments must not affect production services.
Biological construction practice is restricted to institutionally approved, nonpathogenic teaching systems; design proposals do not authorize environmental release.
Provide accessible tools and datasets, document instrument/software versions, and assess reproducibility, uncertainty and limitations rather than treating tool output as ground truth.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Foundations

includes: Cellular life, organization and energy, heredity, variation, evolution and biological evidence.

practice: Interpret organism and cell observations and construct evidence-based explanations separating mechanism from evolutionary history.

outcomes.description: Distinguish evolutionary explanations from purposeful narratives and evaluate basic observational and experimental evidence.
Explain how reproduction transmits information while mutation and recombination generate variation.
Compare cellular organization and levels of biological organization using explicitly introduced matter and energy concepts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations

includes: Variables, expressions, control flow, functions, elementary collections, files, testing and debugging in one general-purpose language.

practice: Build a file-processing application from a specification and submit tests and a debugging record.

outcomes.description: Decompose tasks into functions and manipulate strings, lists, records and files with explicit input contracts.
Trace and write programs using variables, conditionals and loops, including basic numeric and Boolean expressions.
Create tests, inspect state and isolate syntax, runtime and logic errors.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Numerical and algebraic entry for all subjects.

includes: Arithmetic, ratios, units and scientific notation; elementary equations; graphs, powers, exponentials and logarithms.

practice: Solve mixed unit-and-model problems by hand and verify numerical results with a calculator.

outcomes.description: Solve linear, quadratic and elementary exponential equations and rearrange symbolic formulas.
Interpret and construct polynomial, exponential and logarithmic graphs from quantities and data.
Convert units and calculate ratios, percentages and scientific-notation quantities with dimensional checks.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Organismal Diversity

includes: Bacteria, archaea, microbial eukaryotes, fungi, plants and animals; diagnostic traits, life cycles and body plans.

practice: Use identification keys and annotated specimens or images to build a comparative lineage and life-cycle portfolio.

outcomes.description: Compare plant, fungal and animal body plans and relate structural organization to ecological constraints.
Compare reproductive and life-cycle strategies, including haploid/diploid transitions and symbiotic dependencies.
Identify major lineages using diagnostic traits and distinguish classification from superficial resemblance.

decks.subject: chemistry

practice: Solve composition and reaction-accounting problems and prepare a documented dilution plan.

outcomes.description: Relate atoms, isotopes, ions and formulas to mass, charge and composition.
Balance reactions and calculate limiting reagents, yields and mole-to-mass conversions.
Calculate concentration, dilution and ideal-gas quantities with unit and model checks.

decks.subject: computer-science

practice: Build a small processor in a taught logic simulator and trace assembly and cache-access sequences.

outcomes.description: Construct Boolean and sequential circuits and calculate integer and floating-point encodings.
Trace assembly instructions through datapaths and analyze pipeline hazards.
Calculate cache and memory-access behavior and explain locality and hierarchy tradeoffs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures

includes: Arrays, linked structures, stacks/queues, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs and asymptotic operation costs.

practice: Implement interchangeable structures and benchmark workloads while checking invariants and operation counts.

outcomes.description: Calculate asymptotic time and space costs and distinguish worst-case, average and amortized arguments.
Represent graphs with matrices and adjacency structures and implement basic traversals.
Implement hash tables, search trees and heaps and explain collision and balancing tradeoffs.
Implement sequence, stack and queue abstractions while maintaining representation invariants.
