practice: Build a relational application, inspect execution plans and reproduce transaction anomalies in an isolated database.

outcomes.description: Compare index, join and query-plan costs and implement an elementary relational operator.
Design normalized schemas and express queries in relational algebra and SQL with null and multiplicity semantics.
Analyze serializability, isolation anomalies, locking and log-based recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics

includes: Mesh representations, homogeneous transforms, projection, clipping, rasterization, visibility and local shading.

practice: Build a small software renderer and validate transforms, visibility and interpolation against hand-computed scenes.

outcomes.description: Construct mesh and camera representations and calculate homogeneous modeling and projection transforms.
Implement clipping, triangle rasterization, interpolation and depth-buffer visibility.
Implement local reflection and texture models and distinguish geometric, shading and sampling artifacts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Theory

includes: Entropy, divergence, mutual information, source coding and discrete memoryless channel capacity.

practice: Construct codes and compare achievable lengths and error rates with theoretical limits.

outcomes.description: Calculate capacities of elementary channels and reconstruct coding and converse arguments.
Calculate information measures and prove chain rules, nonnegativity and data-processing inequalities.
Construct prefix codes and derive elementary source-coding bounds using typical sequences.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages
decks.description: Formal meaning and design of languages.

includes: Lambda calculus, operational semantics, type judgments, polymorphism, effects, environments and memory management.

practice: Implement a typed interpreter and accompany it with formal rules and selected soundness proofs.

outcomes.description: Implement environments, closures and elementary garbage collection and compare evaluation and effect models.
Define small-step and big-step semantics and prove elementary equivalence and determinism results.
Construct type derivations and prove progress and preservation for a small typed language.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Systems Programming

includes: Pointers, allocation, memory layout, system calls, files, processes, threads and synchronization APIs.

practice: Build a concurrent file-processing service and investigate memory and race failures with taught diagnostic tools.

outcomes.description: Implement thread-safe shared-state programs using locks, condition variables and documented invariants.
Write low-level code with explicit ownership and lifetime rules and diagnose memory errors.
Use process and file APIs with correct resource cleanup and error handling.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus

includes: Limits, derivatives, definite and improper integrals, fundamental theorem and Taylor series at computational depth.

practice: Solve symbolic and graphical modeling problems and compare exact values with Taylor approximations.

outcomes.description: Differentiate composite functions and solve optimization and related-rate problems.
Evaluate integrals using substitution and parts and apply the fundamental theorem to accumulation.
Evaluate elementary limits and interpret continuity and asymptotic behavior.
Test elementary series convergence and use Taylor expansions with remainder estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Category Theory

includes: Categories, functors, natural transformations, limits, representability, Yoneda and adjunctions.

practice: Prove universal properties in several concrete categories and verify naturality diagrams.

outcomes.description: Construct categories, functors and natural transformations using sets, orders and vector spaces.
Prove universal properties of limits, colimits and representable constructions.
Prove the Yoneda lemma and establish adjunctions through natural hom-set correspondences.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Enumerative Combinatorics

includes: Bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions.

practice: Give two independent derivations of counting formulas and reconcile recurrence and generating-function solutions.

outcomes.description: Solve counting problems using bijections, double counting and inclusion-exclusion.
Use formal ordinary and exponential generating functions to extract counting formulas.
Derive and solve combinatorial recurrences with justified initial conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graph Theory

includes: Graph representations, invariants, connectivity, trees, coloring and planarity.

practice: Construct extremal graph examples and write proofs linking local degrees to global structure.

outcomes.description: Establish coloring bounds and test planarity using structural theorems and counterexamples.
Prove tree and connectivity properties and construct paths, cuts and spanning trees.
Translate relational problems into graphs and prove invariant and isomorphism claims.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Group Theory

includes: Groups, homomorphisms, quotients, group actions and Sylow theory.

practice: Classify small groups and prove symmetry-counting results through actions.

outcomes.description: Use orbit-stabilizer, class equations and Sylow theorems to determine finite-group structure.
Prove subgroup and homomorphism properties and classify elementary cyclic and permutation examples.
Construct quotient groups and apply isomorphism theorems with normality checks.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Elementary Number Theory

includes: Divisibility, Euclidean algorithms, congruences, arithmetic functions and quadratic residues.

practice: Solve modular systems by hand and prove number-theoretic claims with explicit exceptional cases.

outcomes.description: Analyze arithmetic functions and quadratic residues and prove elementary prime-distribution statements.
Prove divisibility results and execute Euclidean and extended-Euclidean algorithms.
Solve congruences using modular inverses, exponentiation and the Chinese remainder theorem.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Rings and Fields

includes: Rings, ideals, quotient rings, polynomial arithmetic, factorization and field extensions.

practice: Construct quotient examples and prove irreducibility and extension-degree claims.

outcomes.description: Construct finite and algebraic field extensions and calculate degrees and minimal polynomials.
Test polynomial irreducibility and distinguish Euclidean, principal-ideal and unique-factorization domains.
Construct ideals and quotient rings and prove basic ring-homomorphism and divisibility results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Axiomatic Set Theory

includes: ZF-style axioms, well-foundedness, ordinals, transfinite induction/recursion, cardinals and choice.

practice: Develop transfinite constructions and distinguish ordinal from cardinal arithmetic through proofs.

outcomes.description: Use set axioms to justify constructions and explain how unrestricted comprehension creates paradox.
Compare infinite cardinalities and prove standard equivalences and consequences of choice.
Calculate ordinal operations and prove results by transfinite induction and recursion.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference

includes: Descriptive data analysis, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, common tests and multiplicity procedures.

practice: Analyze supplied datasets with hand checks and documented spreadsheet formulas, including a misleading-significance case.

outcomes.description: Summarize distributions, missingness and outliers using plots, robust summaries and spreadsheet calculations.
Perform t, contingency-table and permutation tests and distinguish effect size, uncertainty and significance.
Construct and interpret mean and proportion intervals using stated sampling assumptions and reference distributions.
Apply familywise and false-discovery-rate procedures and explain their differing error guarantees.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology

includes: Topological and metric spaces, continuity, products, quotients, compactness and connectedness.

practice: Build counterexamples separating topological properties and prove quotient-space descriptions.

outcomes.description: Analyze convergence, completeness and countability in metric spaces, including non-Euclidean examples.
Construct subspace, product and quotient topologies and prove continuity using open sets.
Prove compactness and connectedness results and use invariants to distinguish spaces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum and Nuclear Phenomena

includes: Photoelectric and interference evidence, photon/matter-wave relations, atomic levels and radioactive decay at algebraic depth.

practice: Interpret archived photoelectric, spectral and decay data with algebraic models and explicit model comparisons.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary spectral transitions and distinguish atomic-model predictions from their limitations.
Use photon and de Broglie relations to interpret experiments that defeat classical particle or wave accounts.
Distinguish decay types and calculate activity, half-life and attenuation using exponential models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology

includes: Quadrat/transect/capture-recapture sampling, population growth, species interactions, communities and ecosystem material/energy budgets.

practice: Analyze a field survey with detectability and uncertainty checks and construct a community or ecosystem budget.

outcomes.description: Estimate abundance and diversity using field sampling designs and identify detectability and spatial-sampling bias.
Construct ecosystem energy and nutrient budgets and explain productivity, decomposition and disturbance responses.
Interpret discrete population growth and species-interaction evidence across terrestrial and aquatic communities.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology
decks.description: Mechanisms and evidence of biological change.

includes: Selection, drift, mutation and migration; adaptation; speciation; phylogenetic evidence and comparative historical inference.

practice: Compare evolutionary explanations for supplied population and fossil cases and construct alternative character trees.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary allele-frequency changes and distinguish selection, drift, migration and mutation explanations.
Construct small character-based trees and distinguish homology, convergence and ancestral-state uncertainty.
Evaluate reproductive-isolation and diversification hypotheses using genetic, ecological and fossil evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Measurement and Wet Methods

includes: Chemical safety, weighing, volumetric technique, titrimetry, gravimetry, blanks, standards and calibration uncertainty.

practice: Complete a supervised assay with blanks, replicate preparations, standards and a traceable uncertainty budget.

outcomes.description: Construct standard, blank and standard-addition calibrations and quantify detection limits and uncertainty.
Plan safe handling, storage, waste segregation and emergency responses from hazard information.
Perform or document validated volumetric and gravimetric analyses with stoichiometric endpoint calculations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Coordination Chemistry
decks.description: Structure and reactivity of metal complexes.

includes: Coordination geometry/isomerism, crystal and ligand fields, magnetism, stability, substitution and redox mechanisms.

practice: Determine unknown-complex structures and mechanisms from composition, magnetic, equilibrium and rate evidence.

outcomes.description: Distinguish substitution and electron-transfer pathways and interpret kinetic and thermodynamic evidence.
Determine coordination geometries, isomers, electron counts and complex stability from ligand properties.
Construct ligand-field diagrams and predict spin, magnetism and qualitative electronic spectra.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Reaction Kinetics
decks.description: Rates and mechanisms of chemical change.

includes: Empirical rate laws, integrated kinetics, Arrhenius behavior, elementary mechanisms and steady-state approximations.

practice: Analyze supplied kinetic traces and discriminate mechanisms using derived rate laws and residual plots taught locally.

outcomes.description: Derive and apply integrated zero-, first- and second-order rate laws and half-life relations.
Derive rate predictions from elementary mechanisms using pre-equilibrium and steady-state assumptions.
Estimate reaction orders, rate constants and activation parameters from concentration-time and temperature data.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Main-Group Chemistry

includes: s- and p-block structures, oxidation-state trends, electron-deficient/hypervalent bonding and representative transformations.

practice: Compare unfamiliar main-group compounds and construct balanced reaction networks with justified stability trends.

outcomes.description: Predict representative hydride, oxide, halide and organoelement transformations using bonding, acid-base and redox reasoning.
Explain main-group structural and oxidation-state trends, including inert-pair and electron-deficient behavior.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Solid-State and Materials Chemistry

includes: Crystal lattices, stoichiometric/nonstoichiometric defects, powder diffraction and solid-state synthesis/property relations.

practice: Identify phases from supplied diffraction patterns and propose a preparation route with defect and phase-control checks.

outcomes.description: Describe unit cells and defects and enforce composition and charge balance in nonstoichiometric solids.
Calculate Bragg spacings and index simple powder patterns while distinguishing phase and size effects.
Design solid-state or solution-based preparation routes and relate processing to phase, microstructure and properties.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Stereochemistry

includes: Functional groups, skeletal representations, conformations, stereochemistry, resonance, acidity and elementary electronic effects.

practice: Build molecular models and defend stereochemical, conformational and acidity rankings.

outcomes.description: Translate names, skeletal formulas and three-dimensional representations and identify functional groups.
Assign stereochemical relationships and configurations and compare conformational energies.
Use resonance, induction and acid-base equilibria to predict relative stability and reactive sites.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence

includes: Heuristic/adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, first-order knowledge representation, planning and Bayesian networks.

practice: Build a search-and-planning agent and compare symbolic and probabilistic reasoning on controlled incomplete-information tasks.

outcomes.description: Implement heuristic and adversarial search and prove admissibility or pruning conditions.
Represent knowledge with clauses and constraints and implement unification, resolution and elementary planning.
Construct Bayesian networks and perform exact inference using conditional-independence factorization.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compiler Construction

includes: Lexing/parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, dataflow, optimization and code generation.

practice: Implement an end-to-end compiler for a small language and compare execution against its reference interpreter.

outcomes.description: Generate executable code with register allocation, calling conventions and differential correctness tests.
Build typed intermediate representations and perform dataflow-based, semantics-preserving optimizations.
Construct tokenizers, grammars and parsers and diagnose ambiguity and syntax errors.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computational Complexity

includes: P/NP completeness, space complexity, hierarchy theorems, randomized classes and proof-system perspectives.

practice: Write full hardness proofs and analyze resource bounds and error amplification for randomized procedures.

outcomes.description: Prove NP-completeness and related hardness results with polynomial reductions and certificates.
Compare randomized complexity classes and derive amplification and elementary interactive-proof guarantees.
Analyze space-bounded computation and prove representative hierarchy and simulation results.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptography
decks.description: Construction and proof of cryptographic security.

includes: Security games, pseudorandomness, symmetric encryption/MACs, public-key encryption, signatures and key exchange.

practice: Implement toy constructions for testing and write reduction proofs; distinguish educational code from deployable cryptography.

outcomes.description: Analyze signature and key-exchange protocols, including composition, randomness and misuse failures.
Construct modular-arithmetic public-key schemes and relate security to stated computational assumptions.
Define symmetric security games and prove elementary encryption and authentication reductions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Verification

includes: Hoare logic, invariants, temporal logic, finite-state model checking and interactive theorem proving.

practice: Verify a small stateful component with both deductive proofs and model-checking counterexample analysis.

outcomes.description: Specify temporal properties and implement or execute finite-state model checking with counterexample interpretation.
Derive Hoare-style correctness proofs with loop invariants, termination measures and explicit memory assumptions.
Encode definitions and inductive proofs in a taught proof assistant and identify the trusted computing base.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks

includes: Layered packet protocols, addressing, routing, reliable transport, congestion control and socket measurement.

practice: Build socket applications in a private emulated network and explain packet traces under controlled delay and loss.

outcomes.description: Trace encapsulation, addressing, naming and application exchanges through a packet stack.
Construct forwarding tables and analyze distance-vector and link-state routing behavior.
Implement socket communication and measure retransmission, congestion, bandwidth-delay and loss effects.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems

includes: Scheduling, isolation, virtual memory, file systems, storage recovery, deadlock and synchronization.

practice: Extend a teaching kernel or explicit OS simulator and stress-test scheduling, paging and crash recovery.

outcomes.description: Design elementary file-system structures and explain crash-consistent update and recovery protocols.
Implement scheduling policies and analyze fairness, utilization and process isolation.
Establish synchronization invariants and identify race, deadlock and starvation mechanisms.
Trace address translation and implement page-replacement policies with measured fault behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel Computing

includes: Task/data decomposition, work-span analysis, shared-memory, accelerator and message-passing programming.

practice: Parallelize matrix or stencil kernels in contrasting models and report correctness and scaling experiments.

outcomes.description: Decompose algorithms into dependency graphs and calculate work, span and communication lower bounds.
Implement race-free shared-memory, accelerator and message-passing kernels with explicit synchronization.
Measure strong/weak scaling and diagnose load imbalance, memory bandwidth and communication bottlenecks.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology

includes: Homotopy, fundamental groups, coverings, chain complexes, homology and obstruction applications.

practice: Compute invariants of glued spaces and write complete obstruction proofs.

outcomes.description: Compute fundamental groups and classify elementary covering spaces using lifting and van Kampen methods.
Construct chain complexes and compute simplicial or cellular homology and exact-sequence consequences.
Use homotopy and homology invariants to prove non-equivalence and fixed-point or retraction obstructions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Commutative Algebra

includes: Modules and exact sequences, tensor products, localization, Noetherian rings, prime ideals and dimension.

practice: Compute localizations and ideal decompositions and prove finite-generation and dimension claims.

outcomes.description: Localize rings and modules and use local-global reasoning for ideal and module properties.
Construct module maps, exact sequences and tensor products and prove basic structure results.
Prove Noetherian and integral-extension results and calculate prime chains and elementary Krull dimensions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Ordinary Differential Equations

includes: First-order equations, linear second-order equations and systems, phase portraits, existence conditions and Euler methods.

practice: Compare exact solutions with hand or spreadsheet time-stepping tables for forced and decaying systems.

outcomes.description: Construct Euler and improved-Euler approximations and diagnose step-size error and elementary instability.
Solve constant-coefficient equations and linear systems and classify their phase portraits.
Solve separable and first-order linear equations and check initial conditions and existence hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Experimental Design and Causal Reasoning

includes: Randomization, blocking, factorial contrasts, confounding, causal diagrams and elementary power planning.

practice: Write a preregistered design with randomization scheme, causal assumptions, power calculation and analysis contrasts.

outcomes.description: Use causal diagrams and potential-outcome assumptions to distinguish confounding, mediation and identifiable comparisons.
Calculate sample-size and power approximations from specified effects, variability and error rates.
Design randomized, blocked and factorial comparisons and identify experimental units and interaction contrasts.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Galois Theory

includes: Normal/separable extensions, Galois correspondence, finite fields and solvability by radicals.

practice: Compute splitting fields and subgroup lattices and prove a non-solvability result.

outcomes.description: Determine Galois groups and prove the field-subgroup correspondence for finite Galois extensions.
Use solvable groups and extension towers to determine radical solvability and classical construction obstructions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic

includes: First-order syntax and semantics, formal deduction, completeness, compactness and arithmetic incompleteness.

practice: Write formal derivations, construct nonstandard models by compactness and reconstruct a diagonal proof.

outcomes.description: Explain and reconstruct arithmetization and diagonal arguments establishing incompleteness under stated hypotheses.
Prove completeness using a Henkin construction and apply compactness to model existence.
Construct first-order structures and formal derivations and prove soundness for a specified proof system.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable Calculus

includes: Partial and total derivatives, Jacobians, Hessians, multiple integration and local coordinate theorems.

practice: Construct integration regions and solve constrained local-model problems with explicit coordinate checks.

outcomes.description: Apply stated inverse and implicit function theorems and Lagrange multipliers under checked hypotheses.
Evaluate multiple integrals using geometric bounds and coordinate-change Jacobians.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians and Hessians and apply multivariable chain and Taylor rules.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis

includes: Floating point, conditioning, direct and iterative linear solves, interpolation, quadrature and nonlinear root finding.

practice: Implement algorithms without black-box solvers and report accuracy-versus-cost on well- and ill-conditioned examples.

outcomes.description: Implement interpolation and numerical quadrature and derive elementary approximation-error bounds.
Distinguish conditioning, truncation and roundoff and construct forward/backward error estimates.
Implement bracketed and Newton-type root solvers and justify local convergence and stopping criteria.
Implement pivoted factorization and stationary iterative solvers and diagnose convergence and residual reliability.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis

includes: Completeness, sequences and series, compactness, continuity, rigorous calculus and uniform convergence.

practice: Produce theorem proofs and counterexample portfolios, including failures of limit interchange.

outcomes.description: Prove continuity, compactness and intermediate/extreme-value results in real metric settings.
Prove central differentiation and Riemann-integration theorems under explicit hypotheses.
Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence and justify or refute interchanges of limits, derivatives and integrals.
Prove convergence and completeness results using epsilon arguments and construct divergent counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Regression and Generalized Linear Models

includes: Matrix least squares, logistic and Poisson regression, weighted iterative fitting, diagnostics and prediction.

practice: Build matrix worksheets for least squares and IRLS, then compare predictions and residual diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Fit logistic and Poisson models with explicitly taught iteratively reweighted least squares and interpret links and coefficients.
Fit linear models using design matrices and calculate coefficient and prediction uncertainty.
Diagnose residual structure, collinearity, influential observations and predictive miscalibration using held-out data.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Representation Theory

includes: Finite-group representations, invariant subspaces, Maschke and Schur theorems, characters and tensor products.

practice: Construct character tables and verify decomposition multiplicities for concrete symmetry groups.

outcomes.description: Build character tables and decompose induced and tensor-product representations using orthogonality.
Prove decomposition results and construct irreducible representations and intertwining maps.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Applied Stochastic Models

includes: Finite Markov chains, continuous-time chains, exponential waiting times, Poisson processes and elementary queues.

practice: Solve transition and balance equations by hand and construct spreadsheet event tables using taught inverse-exponential sampling.

outcomes.description: Construct generators and exponential waiting-time models and solve elementary continuous-time event probabilities.
Calculate finite-chain transition, stationary, absorption and hitting-time quantities.
Calculate elementary queue performance and check stationarity and Little-law assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Signals and Integral Transforms

includes: Fourier series/transforms, Laplace transforms, convolution, linear-system response and sampling.

practice: Compute spectra and convolution responses by hand and reconstruct short sampled signals without programming prerequisites.

outcomes.description: Calculate Fourier representations and interpret spectra, symmetry and elementary convergence conditions.
Use Laplace transforms and convolution to solve linear response and initial-value problems.
Derive elementary sampling and aliasing relationships and calculate discrete Fourier coefficients for short records.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics

includes: Vector kinematics, Newton laws, force models, conservation laws, rotation, gravitation and elementary orbits.

practice: Solve multirepresentation mechanics problems and test a conservation prediction with video or supervised apparatus.

outcomes.description: Apply work-energy and momentum conservation to collisions and variable-force problems.
Calculate gravitational fields, effective orbital energies and elementary circular/Keplerian relations.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve translational motion with constraints and friction.
Calculate torques, moments of inertia and angular momentum for rigid-body motion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Biology

includes: Ethograms and behavioral sampling, proximate/ultimate explanations, foraging/mating models, learning and social behavior.

practice: Code approved or archived behavioral observations and evaluate competing mechanistic and adaptive hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Evaluate foraging, mating and kin-selection hypotheses using explicitly taught cost-benefit and inclusive-fitness models.
Construct ethograms and unbiased behavioral sampling protocols with observer-agreement checks.
Distinguish learning, social transmission and communication mechanisms through controlled behavioral comparisons.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biochemistry

includes: Protein, nucleic-acid, lipid and carbohydrate structure; folding, binding equilibria and algebraic enzyme kinetics.

practice: Interpret binding and enzyme datasets with algebraic models and propose molecular explanations for altered activity.

outcomes.description: Calculate fractional occupancy and dissociation constants and distinguish affinity, cooperativity and binding specificity.
Relate biomolecular sequence, stereochemistry and noncovalent interactions to folding, assembly and function.
Interpret catalytic mechanisms and Michaelis-Menten/inhibition curves using explicitly stated steady-state assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology

includes: Membranes and transport, organelles and trafficking, cytoskeleton, cell cycle and microscopy-image interpretation.

practice: Annotate cell images and predict localization, transport and division phenotypes from defined molecular perturbations.

outcomes.description: Explain cell-cycle transitions and checkpoints and interpret perturbations of division control.
Relate cytoskeletal polymers and motors to cell shape, movement and image-based organization.
Explain membrane structure and predict passive, facilitated and active transport from molecular and gradient conditions.
Trace protein and membrane trafficking and infer organelle defects from localization evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology

includes: Biodiversity threats, fragmentation, genetic diversity, reserve/restoration planning and adaptive management under uncertainty.

practice: Develop a conservation decision dossier with competing interventions, monitoring design and explicit ecological tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Design adaptive monitoring and intervention comparisons that separate management effects from background change.
Assess biodiversity loss and distinguish habitat, exploitation, invasive-species and climate mechanisms using evidence.
Compare reserve, connectivity and restoration alternatives using transparent biological criteria and uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology

includes: Incidence/prevalence and risk, epidemiological designs, bias, censoring, outbreak curves and compartmental transmission models.

practice: Analyze an anonymized cohort and outbreak dataset and compare observed patterns with a documented compartment model.

outcomes.description: Estimate rates, risks and adjusted associations and diagnose selection, measurement and confounding bias.
Construct Kaplan-Meier estimates and outbreak summaries with censoring, denominators and ascertainment assumptions checked.
Derive and time-step elementary SIR models and calculate reproduction thresholds and intervention sensitivities.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Phylogenetics and Systematics

includes: Sequence substitution, tree likelihood/pruning, topology search, support and phylogenetic comparative models.

practice: Implement a small phylogenetic likelihood calculation and compare tree and trait inferences under alternative models.

outcomes.description: Fit locally derived phylogenetic covariance models and distinguish shared ancestry from independent trait association.
Construct continuous-time substitution models and calculate sequence-transition and tree-likelihood probabilities.
Implement likelihood pruning and bounded topology search and assess branch support and model misspecification.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population and Quantitative Genetics

includes: Selection/migration/mutation/drift recursions, linkage disequilibrium, coalescent models and quantitative-genetic response.

practice: Derive population and coalescent predictions and analyze supplied genetic-variance and demographic datasets.

outcomes.description: Derive deterministic and finite-population allele-frequency models and analyze equilibrium, drift and linkage effects.
Derive elementary coalescent waiting-time and diversity predictions and evaluate demographic-identifiability limits.
Estimate additive genetic variance and derive multivariate response-to-selection predictions with environmental assumptions explicit.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative Ecology

includes: Population/interactions dynamics, local stability, stage-structured demography, occupancy/count models and model selection.

practice: Analyze demographic and repeated-survey data with matrix, ODE and detection-aware statistical models.

outcomes.description: Construct stage-structured projection matrices and calculate growth, sensitivity and extinction-risk approximations.
Construct population and interaction ODEs and analyze equilibria and local Jacobian stability using derivatives taught locally.
Fit ecological count and occupancy models with explicit detection processes and evaluate predictive and mechanistic adequacy.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

includes: Aquatic/soil/atmospheric speciation, partitioning, adsorption, transformation, compartment balances and environmental sampling.

practice: Analyze a watershed or atmospheric-box case with chemical balances, uncertainty and a defensible sampling plan.

outcomes.description: Construct compartment mass balances and predict partitioning, adsorption and transformation using taught isotherm and rate models.
Design environmental chemical sampling with preservation, blanks, recovery controls and detection-limit interpretation.
Calculate environmental acid-base, metal and redox speciation under stated equilibrium assumptions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Analysis

includes: UV-visible and atomic analysis, chromatography, mass spectrometry, introductory IR and NMR interpretation.

practice: Analyze a blinded mixture using supplied instrument records or supervised instruments and justify identification and quantification.

outcomes.description: Calculate chromatographic retention, efficiency and resolution and choose defensible separation conditions.
Interpret ionization, mass-to-charge and isotope/fragment patterns and assess mass-spectral identification limits.
Select optical analytical methods and calculate calibrated concentrations while diagnosing matrix and spectral interference.
Use locally taught IR bands and NMR shift, integration and coupling rules to constrain small-molecule structures.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms

includes: Electron-flow mechanisms for substitution/elimination, unsaturated additions, carbonyl, aromatic, radical and elementary pericyclic reactions.

practice: Solve unseen mechanism and product problems, rejecting alternatives through charge, orbital and stereochemical checks.

outcomes.description: Construct alkene and alkyne addition mechanisms and predict regioselectivity and stereoselectivity.
Predict aromatic substitution pathways and directing effects using resonance and aromaticity arguments.
Construct carbonyl addition, acyl substitution and enolate mechanisms with acid-base consistency.
Distinguish radical-chain and elementary pericyclic pathways and predict products using taught orbital-phase rules.
Predict substitution and elimination pathways and stereochemical outcomes from substrate and conditions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Radiochemistry

includes: Radioisotope activity/counting, decay chains, chemical yield, radiochemical separation and isotope tracing.

practice: Analyze archived counting and recovery data and design a tracer study with explicit radiation-control requirements.

outcomes.description: Interpret tracer dilution and labeling experiments while distinguishing isotope exchange and chemical transformation.
Design isotope separation and recovery controls using chemical selectivity and contamination accounting.
Calculate activity, efficiency-corrected counts and elementary parent-daughter decay with uncertainty.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems

includes: Logical clocks, distributed snapshots, replicated state, consistency, consensus and failure models.

practice: Implement a replicated log and test delayed, duplicated, reordered and dropped messages against explicit invariants.

outcomes.description: Derive consensus safety arguments and explain liveness limitations under crash, partition and Byzantine models.
Reason about causal and total order and implement clocks and consistent snapshots.
Implement replicated-state mechanisms and distinguish linearizable, sequential and eventual consistency.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluation of usable systems.

includes: User research, task models, interaction design, accessibility, prototyping and mixed-method usability evaluation.

practice: Iterate an accessible prototype through consented or simulated user studies and document design changes and evidence.

outcomes.description: Conduct ethically scoped interviews and task analyses and synthesize requirements without overgeneralizing qualitative evidence.
Build accessible interactive prototypes using feedback, affordance and error-recovery principles.
Design usability studies and interpret behavioral metrics, qualitative observations and uncertainty.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning

includes: Predictive models, trees, clustering, PCA, empirical risk, gradient/SGD training, regularization and evaluation.

practice: Implement core learners and training loops and submit reproducible held-out evaluation with ablations and leakage checks.

outcomes.description: Design leakage-resistant validation and measure calibration, subgroup errors and distribution-shift failures.
Derive empirical-loss gradients and implement batch and stochastic-gradient training with regularization.
Implement linear, logistic, nearest-neighbor and tree predictors and compare their inductive assumptions.
Implement k-means and principal-component methods and interpret clustering and projection limitations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Physically Based Rendering

includes: Radiometry, bidirectional scattering, rendering equation and Monte Carlo light transport.

practice: Build a small path tracer and validate energy conservation and Monte Carlo error against analytic scenes.

outcomes.description: Derive radiometric light-transport equations with correct measures, units and scattering constraints.
Implement path tracing and importance sampling and quantify estimator bias, variance and convergence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics

includes: Rigid transformations and robot Jacobians, Bayesian state estimation, feedback stability and collision-aware planning.

practice: Implement estimation and feedback for a simulated robot and test sensor noise, saturation and obstacle failures.

outcomes.description: Design feedback and collision-aware motion plans and assess local closed-loop stability and model mismatch.
Derive forward/inverse kinematics and velocity Jacobians for articulated and mobile robots.
Derive and implement Kalman and extended-Kalman updates with covariance and observability checks taught locally.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Security

includes: Threat models, access control, memory and input vulnerabilities, isolation, authentication and defensive monitoring.

practice: Audit and harden an intentionally vulnerable isolated service, documenting authorization, evidence and mitigation tests.

outcomes.description: Configure authenticated network services and evaluate isolation, logging and incident evidence under stated threats.
Diagnose memory, injection and authorization flaws in teaching programs and implement tested mitigations.
Construct threat models and justify least-privilege, trust-boundary and access-control designs.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Geometry

includes: Affine/projective varieties, Zariski topology, Nullstellensatz, morphisms, local rings and singularities.

practice: Analyze explicit curves and surfaces algebraically, including projective closure and singular points.

outcomes.description: Use local rings and tangent spaces to determine dimension and elementary singularities.
Construct projective varieties and analyze homogeneous equations and affine charts.
Use the ideal-variety correspondence and Zariski topology to determine irreducibility and morphisms.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Theory and methods of complex functions.

includes: Holomorphic functions, Cauchy theory, analytic continuation and residues.

practice: Write contour proofs and evaluate real integrals while checking poles, branch choices and limiting arcs.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Cauchy integral results with domain and regularity hypotheses.
Test holomorphicity and establish power-series and analytic-continuation properties.
Classify singularities and use residues and the argument principle to evaluate integrals and count zeros.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry

includes: Smooth manifolds, tangent/cotangent spaces, tensors, differential forms, metrics, connections and curvature.

practice: Calculate tensors and geodesics in multiple charts and prove coordinate invariance of selected constructions.

outcomes.description: Compute metric connections, geodesics and curvature and relate them to intrinsic geometry.
Calculate exterior derivatives, pullbacks and integrals of forms and apply manifold Stokes theorems.
Construct smooth charts, tangent maps and tensor-coordinate transformations on manifolds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Dynamical Systems

includes: Flows and maps, Lyapunov stability, invariant sets, local bifurcations and deterministic chaos.

practice: Prove stability claims and construct bifurcation diagrams using analytic reductions and tabulated iterations.

outcomes.description: Derive normal forms and classify saddle-node, pitchfork and Hopf bifurcations.
Analyze symbolic dynamics, sensitive dependence and Lyapunov growth in representative maps.
Prove local stability and invariant-set results using linearization and Lyapunov functions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Integration

includes: Sigma-algebras, measure construction, Lebesgue integration, convergence, product and signed measures.

practice: Prove integration theorems and construct examples where domination or absolute integrability fails.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply monotone, dominated and Fatou convergence results for Lebesgue integrals.
Construct measures from outer measures and prove measurability and approximation results.
Apply Tonelli, Fubini and Radon-Nikodym theorems under verified hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Continuous Optimization

includes: Linear-programming geometry and duality; convex optimality; constrained and unconstrained numerical iterations.

practice: Solve primal-dual problems and compare hand-computed iterations against optimality certificates.

outcomes.description: Establish convexity and derive subgradient and KKT optimality conditions with constraint qualifications.
Formulate linear programs, perform small simplex calculations and prove weak and strong duality in standard settings.
Execute gradient, Newton and projected iterations and derive representative descent and convergence guarantees.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Vector Calculus

includes: Gradient, divergence, curl, line and surface integrals, Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems.

practice: Calculate the same flux or circulation by direct integration and by an applicable integral theorem.

outcomes.description: Parameterize curves and surfaces and calculate oriented circulation and flux.
Calculate differential field operators and distinguish conservative and solenoidal fields.
Apply and justify integral theorems for regular domains, including orientation and singularity checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

includes: Variational calculus, generalized coordinates, constraints, Lagrangians, Hamiltonians, canonical transformations and Noether symmetry.

practice: Derive and solve one mechanical system in Newtonian, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and elementary canonical transformations and analyze phase-space dynamics.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from stationary action and solve constrained mechanical models.
Derive conservation laws from continuous symmetries and distinguish symmetry from coordinate coincidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics

includes: Physical time integration, symplectic methods, random-number sampling, Monte Carlo integration and computational verification.

practice: Implement an orbital simulator and Monte Carlo observable calculation with convergence, conservation and reproducibility tests.

outcomes.description: Validate simulations against exact limits, dimensional scaling, refinement and independent implementations.
Implement Runge-Kutta and symplectic mechanical integrators and analyze conservation and long-time error.
Implement inverse-transform and rejection sampling and Monte Carlo integration with uncertainty estimates.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Magnetism

includes: Coulomb/Gauss electrostatics, potential/capacitance, DC and elementary transient circuits, magnetic forces and induction.

practice: Solve field and circuit problems and characterize a low-voltage circuit with explicit instrument and safety checks.

outcomes.description: Solve Kirchhoff circuit equations and derive elementary RC transients by separation of variables taught locally.
Calculate induced emf, inductive energy and elementary electromagnetic energy transfer with sign checks.
Calculate symmetric charge fields, potentials and capacitances using superposition and elementary Gauss arguments.
Calculate magnetic fields in standard geometries and charged-particle or current forces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Special Relativity

includes: Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals, simultaneity, four-momentum and relativistic collisions.

practice: Solve frame-dependent descriptions of the same event and verify invariant energy-momentum results.

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations, intervals and time-order relations using spacetime diagrams.
Use four-momentum conservation to solve relativistic collision, decay and threshold problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermodynamics

includes: Thermodynamic laws, reversible/irreversible processes, engines, potentials, Maxwell relations, response and stability.

practice: Analyze thermodynamic cycles and derive response identities and stability inequalities from explicit potentials.

outcomes.description: Use entropy and free-energy extrema to determine equilibrium, stability and phase-coexistence conditions.
Apply thermodynamic laws to reversible and irreversible processes and derive engine-efficiency limits.
Construct thermodynamic potentials and derive Maxwell and response-function relations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Oscillations and Waves

includes: Free, damped and driven oscillators, coupled modes, traveling/standing waves, interference and wave-energy transport.

practice: Analyze resonance and standing-wave measurements and compare amplitude/phase data with analytic models.

outcomes.description: Calculate interference, beats and wave intensity and relate energy transport to oscillation amplitude.
Derive oscillator amplitude, phase and resonance and calculate coupled normal modes.
Construct traveling and standing-wave solutions and apply boundary, phase and group-speed relations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Metabolism
decks.description: Energy and matter through biochemical networks.

includes: ATP/redox accounting, glycolysis, respiration, photosynthetic energy conversion, biosynthesis and metabolic regulation.

practice: Solve isotope and energy-accounting cases and predict metabolite changes under defined nutritional and enzyme perturbations.

outcomes.description: Explain major biosynthetic routes and integrate allosteric, hormonal and compartmental regulation across metabolic states.
Trace central catabolic and photosynthetic energy-conversion pathways and predict consequences of blocked steps.
Balance carbon, reducing equivalents and ATP and evaluate coupled-reaction free-energy direction.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Genetics

includes: DNA replication/repair/recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and prokaryotic/eukaryotic gene regulation.

practice: Interpret mutation, reporter and rescue experiments and construct falsifiable gene-regulatory explanations.

outcomes.description: Explain DNA maintenance mechanisms and predict mutation and repair phenotypes from molecular lesions.
Trace gene expression through RNA processing and translation and predict sequence-to-product consequences.
Compare regulatory logic across organisms and infer transcriptional, chromatin and post-transcriptional control from perturbations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology

includes: Diffraction/phasing, cryo-EM projection/reconstruction, NMR restraints, model refinement and structural validation.

practice: Analyze supplied diffraction, cryo-EM and NMR-derived records and validate alternative structural models in a documented viewer workflow.

outcomes.description: Use the projection-slice relation to explain cryo-EM alignment/reconstruction and diagnose heterogeneity and resolution artifacts.
Relate diffraction intensities, phases and electron density and explain crystallographic phasing and refinement workflows.
Translate assigned NMR proximity and coupling observations into structural restraints and evaluate underdetermination.
Evaluate molecular models against maps/restraints, geometry and held-out validation using taught molecular-viewer operations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis

includes: Retrosynthesis, functional-group interconversion, protecting groups, stereocontrol, purification and structural verification.

practice: Prepare a justified synthesis dossier and execute an approved small-scale route or analyze archived reaction records.

outcomes.description: Plan purification and verify proposed products using combined spectra, yield and purity evidence.
Develop and compare multistep retrosynthetic routes using strategic disconnections and accessible precursors.
Choose chemoselective and stereoselective conditions and justify protecting-group and order-of-operation decisions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry and Catalysis

includes: Metal-carbon bonding, electron counting, elementary organometallic steps and homogeneous catalytic mechanisms.

practice: Prepare a mechanism dossier comparing catalytic proposals against kinetics, isotope labels and selectivity.

outcomes.description: Build and discriminate catalytic cycles using resting states, rate laws, labeling and deactivation evidence.
Construct oxidative-addition, reductive-elimination, insertion and elimination mechanisms with stereochemical predictions.
Analyze organometallic bonding, electron counts and ligand effects on reactive intermediates.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

includes: Chemical potentials, partial molar quantities, activities/fugacities, solution models and phase equilibria.

practice: Derive and calculate binary-mixture coexistence and compare ideal and nonideal predictions with phase data.

outcomes.description: Derive chemical-potential and partial-molar relations and connect reaction Gibbs energy to equilibrium.
Calculate nonideal mixture properties using activities, fugacities and excess free-energy models.
Construct phase diagrams and solve coexistence conditions using chemical potentials and phase-rule constraints.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision

includes: Image formation and convolution, camera geometry, feature matching, multiview inference and visual recognition.

practice: Implement a calibrated two-view reconstruction and a recognition pipeline with held-out geometric and statistical tests.

outcomes.description: Model image formation and implement spatial/frequency filtering while accounting for sampling and noise.
Estimate camera and multiview geometry using correspondences, least squares and robust consensus fitting taught locally.
Build recognition or segmentation systems and evaluate geometric, domain-shift and subgroup failure modes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Deep Learning
decks.description: Mechanisms and practice of neural learning.

includes: Tensor computation, reverse-mode differentiation, convolutional/recurrent/attention architectures and training diagnostics.

practice: Build a small autodifferentiation engine and train contrasting architectures with compute, data and error audits.

outcomes.description: Implement reverse-mode automatic differentiation on a computation graph and verify gradients numerically.
Diagnose optimization, normalization, overfitting and robustness failures using controlled training experiments.
Construct convolutional, recurrent and attention models and derive their tensor shapes and parameter sharing.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Reinforcement Learning

includes: Markov decision processes, Bellman equations, dynamic programming, temporal-difference learning and policy gradients.

practice: Compare policy-learning methods in controlled simulators with multiple seeds, uncertainty intervals and reward-misspecification tests.

outcomes.description: Formulate discounted Markov decision processes and prove Bellman contraction and policy-improvement results.
Design sequential evaluations addressing exploration, off-policy bias, variance and unsafe reward specification.
Implement value iteration, temporal-difference and policy-gradient methods and derive their update objectives.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Verified Distributed Systems

includes: Abstract-to-implementation refinement, verified safety/liveness assumptions and systematic distributed fault exploration.

practice: Verify and fault-test a bounded replicated protocol, reporting abstraction gaps and trusted components.

outcomes.description: Generate adversarial schedules and fault traces and reconcile experimental counterexamples with proof assumptions.
Construct a machine-checked refinement argument linking a distributed implementation to an abstract state-machine specification.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Analytic Number Theory

includes: Arithmetic Dirichlet series, Euler products, analytic continuation and classical prime-distribution methods.

practice: Write a theorem-focused exposition with full analytic estimates and numerical sanity checks using supplied tables.

outcomes.description: Derive Euler products and continuation properties for zeta and elementary Dirichlet L-functions.
Reconstruct classical arguments connecting zeros, character sums and prime-counting asymptotics.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Discrete Optimization

includes: Flows and matching, integer formulations, branch-and-bound, cutting planes and relaxation bounds.

practice: Produce feasible solutions and independently checkable bounds for scheduling and network instances.

outcomes.description: Formulate integer programs and execute branch-and-bound and valid-cut procedures on small instances.
Solve network flow and matching problems and prove optimality using cut and integrality certificates.
Construct linear and Lagrangian relaxations and quantify integrality gaps and approximation bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis

includes: Banach/Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded and compact operators, weak convergence and variational existence.

practice: Prove operator results and formulate a weak elliptic problem with a complete existence argument.

outcomes.description: Prove completeness, projection and duality results for standard function spaces.
Apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and compact self-adjoint spectral theory with hypotheses verified.
Use weak convergence, Sobolev-space definitions and coercive bilinear forms to prove variational existence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations

includes: Classical heat, wave and Laplace equations; characteristics; separation, eigenfunction and Green-function methods.

practice: Derive solutions for contrasting boundary conditions and test uniqueness with energy arguments taught locally.

outcomes.description: Solve standard linear boundary-value problems using separation, eigenfunction expansions and Green functions.
Solve first-order transport equations by characteristics and identify crossing and shock formation.
Classify elementary PDEs and determine compatible initial/boundary data and well-posedness expectations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability Theory

includes: Measure-theoretic probability, joint laws, conditional expectation, characteristic functions and limit theorems.

practice: Prove limit results and construct random-variable sequences separating convergence modes.

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectations and prove tower, projection and conditional-independence properties.
Distinguish convergence modes and prove representative laws of large numbers and central limit results.
Construct random variables and joint laws and calculate transformed distributions using measure-theoretic definitions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Continuum Mechanics

includes: Continuum fields, deformation/strain tensors, stress, conservation balances and linear elastic constitutive laws.

practice: Derive balances from control volumes and solve stress/deformation problems with constitutive and dimensional checks.

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances and apply stress and traction boundary conditions.
Construct deformation, strain and velocity-gradient tensors and distinguish material from spatial descriptions.
Use linear elastic constitutive laws to solve elementary deformation and elastic-wave problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics

includes: Sensors, amplifiers and transfer functions, noise, digitization, DFT implementation, calibration and model comparison.

practice: Build or emulate a calibrated acquisition chain and submit code, raw data and an uncertainty-aware physical inference report.

outcomes.description: Acquire sampled signals and implement discrete spectral analysis with aliasing, window and quantization checks.
Estimate physical parameters and compare models with propagated uncertainty, residuals and systematic-error tests.
Model sensor/amplifier transfer, loading and noise and design calibrated measurement chains.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity

includes: Lorentzian geometry, equivalence principle, stress-energy, Einstein equations, classical tests, black holes and gravitational waves.

practice: Compute geodesics and curvature for specified metrics and derive observable predictions with weak-field checks.

outcomes.description: Construct stress-energy tensors and derive or verify symmetric Einstein-equation solutions.
Calculate weak-field tests, black-hole observables and linearized gravitational-wave effects.
Calculate Lorentzian intervals, geodesics and local inertial descriptions in curved spacetimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Optics

includes: Ray optics, imaging, interference, diffraction, resolution and polarization.

practice: Design an imaging or diffraction measurement and compare observed patterns with analytic predictions.

outcomes.description: Calculate slit/grating interference and diffraction and quantify resolution limits.
Trace rays through mirrors and lenses and calculate imaging, magnification and elementary aberration effects.
Represent polarization states and calculate polarizer and waveplate transformations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

includes: Wavefunctions, operators, measurement, one-dimensional Schrodinger systems, oscillator algebra, spin and tensor-product states.

practice: Solve quantum models analytically and compare wavefunction, matrix and measurement representations.

outcomes.description: Normalize states and calculate measurement probabilities, expectations, commutators and uncertainty relations.
Solve standard bound and scattering-barrier Schrodinger models and derive harmonic-oscillator spectra.
Calculate spin measurements and tensor-product states and distinguish entanglement from classical correlation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics

includes: Microcanonical/canonical/grand ensembles, fluctuations, classical gases, quantum occupancy statistics and phase transitions.

practice: Derive ensemble predictions for gases and spin systems and compare finite-size and thermodynamic-limit behavior.

outcomes.description: Analyze interacting spin models using mean-field and scaling arguments and identify their critical limitations.
Derive ensemble distributions and calculate partition functions, thermodynamic observables and fluctuations.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupancy distributions from explicitly introduced indistinguishability assumptions and apply ideal-gas limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology

includes: Comparative animal tissues/organs, circulation/respiration, digestion/excretion, endocrine/reproductive regulation and homeostatic failure.

practice: Analyze comparative anatomy and physiological time-series cases using explicitly taught flow, clearance and feedback calculations.

outcomes.description: Use pressure-flow, diffusion and gas-binding models taught locally to explain circulation and respiration.
Explain endocrine feedback and reproductive cycles and predict outcomes of defined hormonal perturbations.
Interpret physiological measurements to distinguish compensatory feedback from organ-system failure without making clinical diagnoses.
Apply mass-balance and gradient reasoning to digestion, nutrient absorption, renal clearance and osmoregulation.
Identify major tissues and organs and relate comparative anatomy to physiological function.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biophysics

includes: Biomolecular free-energy landscapes, polymer elasticity, membrane curvature/transport and single-molecule kinetic inference.

practice: Derive and compare physical models for folding, membrane or single-molecule datasets with parameter and resolution limits explicit.

outcomes.description: Derive folding, binding and polymer-force predictions from partition functions and energy-landscape models.
Apply locally developed membrane curvature-energy and transport models to deformation and permeability measurements.
Infer state kinetics from single-molecule dwell times and force measurements with missed-event and heterogeneity checks.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Formation and transformation of biological form.

includes: Fate specification, morphogens, gene-regulatory patterning, morphogenesis, regeneration and lineage/perturbation experiments.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage and perturbation data and propose discriminating follow-up experiments.

outcomes.description: Explain competence, induction and positional information and infer fate-control networks from perturbations.
Design and interpret lineage-tracing, transplantation and temporal perturbation experiments with appropriate controls.
Relate adhesion, polarity and cell mechanics to morphogenesis, organogenesis and regeneration.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Experimental Biological Methods

includes: Biological controls, pipetting and asepsis, extraction/PCR/electrophoresis, microscopy, assay normalization and reproducible records.

practice: Complete an approved molecular or imaging investigation with controls, raw records, quantitative analysis and a failure audit.

outcomes.description: Acquire or analyze calibrated microscopy images with resolution, segmentation and sampling limitations documented.
Design biological experiments with controls, replication, blinding and contamination-aware sample handling.
Plan and perform approved extraction, amplification and separation assays and diagnose control failures.
Maintain sample provenance and reproducible spreadsheet analyses with normalization and exclusion decisions justified.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics

includes: Sequence alignment and assembly, read quality, variant inference, gene expression, enrichment and reproducible genomic workflows.

practice: Implement a sequence method and complete an archived genomic analysis with controls, provenance and independent validation.

outcomes.description: Build reproducible genomic workflows with reference versions, provenance, validation and privacy-aware data handling.
Analyze normalized expression and enrichment data with experimental-unit, batch and multiplicity controls.
Analyze read quality and infer variants using locally taught read-error likelihoods and mapping-bias checks.
Implement sequence alignment and elementary overlap/de Bruijn assembly and explain scoring and ambiguity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology

includes: Innate sensing, antigen presentation, lymphocyte diversity/selection, immune memory, tolerance and immune assays.

practice: Analyze immune-response and assay datasets, including false-positive, gating and tolerance-failure cases.

outcomes.description: Trace antigen presentation, receptor diversification and lymphocyte activation through adaptive and memory responses.
Interpret immunoassay and flow-cytometry readouts using locally taught gating, controls and specificity checks.
Explain tolerance, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and immune deficiency using cellular mechanisms.
Explain innate sensing, inflammation and complement and predict their tissue-level consequences.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology

includes: Bacterial, archaeal and microbial-eukaryotic physiology; growth/media/asepsis; identification, biofilms and microbial ecology.

practice: Characterize an approved teaching microorganism or archived culture dataset using growth, microscopy and identification evidence.

outcomes.description: Explain biofilm, symbiotic and biogeochemical functions and distinguish culture-based from community-sequence evidence.
Design approved aseptic cultivation and dilution-count measurements and calculate growth and viable counts.
Compare microbial cellular, metabolic and genetic strategies and use diagnostic traits to identify major groups.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Integrated structure and function of plants.

includes: Plant anatomy, water/mineral and sugar transport, photosynthetic physiology, hormones, development, reproduction and stress.

practice: Interpret plant transport and gas-exchange datasets and design an approved growth-response experiment.

outcomes.description: Compare C3, C4 and CAM physiology and interpret photosynthetic and respiratory response curves.
Explain hormonal and environmental control of plant growth, flowering and reproductive development.
Predict drought, salinity, nutrient and biotic-stress responses and distinguish acclimation from adaptation.
Relate plant tissue structure to water potential, mineral acquisition and source-sink transport.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Signaling and Cancer Biology
decks.description: Cellular regulation and its pathological breakdown.

includes: Receptor signaling, pathway cross-talk, cell-fate control, apoptosis, tissue homeostasis and cancer evolution.

practice: Interpret signaling and tumor-perturbation datasets and distinguish causal pathway effects from correlated markers.

outcomes.description: Relate oncogenic alterations, genome instability and microenvironmental selection to tumor progression and resistance.
Explain cell-death, senescence and tissue-homeostasis mechanisms and distinguish their experimental signatures.
Infer receptor-to-effector pathway organization from dose, time and epistasis perturbation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology

includes: Biological network representations, mechanistic ODE models, flux-balance analysis, sensitivity and identifiability.

practice: Implement a gene/metabolic model, fit synthetic and archived observations and design measurements that distinguish competing mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Construct and implement biochemical ODE networks and analyze feedback, steady states and parameter sensitivity.
Build stoichiometric flux-balance models and interpret feasibility, objectives and alternative optima.
Estimate bounded model parameters and distinguish structural nonidentifiability, practical uncertainty and model discrepancy.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Virology
decks.description: Mechanisms and measurement of viral systems.

includes: Viral genome strategies, entry/replication/assembly, host range, viral evolution and infectivity/genome assays.

practice: Analyze archived lifecycle and assay data and propose non-operational discriminating tests of replication hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Explain host range, persistence and viral evolutionary tradeoffs using receptor and population evidence.
Interpret plaque, endpoint-dilution and genome-copy measurements and distinguish infectivity from molecular detection.
Compare viral genome-to-replication strategies and predict host machinery and lifecycle dependencies.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry

includes: Nernst equilibria, electrochemical cells, interfacial charge, Butler-Volmer kinetics and diffusion-limited measurements.

practice: Analyze polarization and voltammetry data, separating equilibrium, kinetic, resistance and transport contributions.

outcomes.description: Use locally derived one-dimensional diffusion-flux and limiting-current models to interpret voltammetric measurements.
Derive electrode potentials and cell free energies with activity and reference-electrode conventions.
Interpret exchange currents, overpotentials and Butler-Volmer/Tafel behavior with mechanism limitations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Medicinal Chemistry

includes: Binding and structure-activity relationships, dose-response, exposure, metabolism, selectivity and lead optimization.

practice: Prepare a lead-optimization proposal from supplied activity, exposure and synthesis data without clinical recommendations.

outcomes.description: Use locally taught clearance, partitioning and metabolic-liability models to evaluate exposure and selectivity tradeoffs.
Propose synthetically feasible lead modifications and design discriminating chemical and biological validation.
Analyze structure-activity and dose-response data while distinguishing potency, efficacy and assay artifacts.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Physical Chemical Kinetics

includes: Transition-state theory, master/rate equations, network timescales, diffusion-controlled reaction models.

practice: Derive rate predictions and analyze competing reaction networks using partition-function and concentration-time evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary diffusion-controlled encounter rates from steady radial flux and compare transport versus activation control.
Construct reaction-network equations and analyze steady states, timescale separation and kinetic identifiability.
Derive transition-state rate expressions from partition functions and evaluate their recrossing and tunneling limitations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

includes: Step/chain-growth polymerization, molecular-weight distributions, chain statistics and polymer solution/phase behavior.

practice: Design a target polymer and analyze conversion, distribution and phase data against explicit synthesis models.

outcomes.description: Calculate number/weight averages and dispersity and interpret size-exclusion and chain-statistical measurements.
Apply locally developed chain-entropy and Flory-Huggins models to predict polymer mixing and phase separation.
Compare step-growth, radical and controlled-chain polymerizations and calculate conversion-dependent chain lengths.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular Hamiltonians, variational orbitals, Hartree-Fock and electron-correlation foundations.

practice: Derive small-basis molecular calculations by hand and compare approximate energies with supplied reference results.

outcomes.description: Distinguish exchange, static and dynamic correlation and explain configuration-interaction and density-functional approximations.
Construct molecular Hamiltonians and justify Born-Oppenheimer and elementary orbital approximations.
Derive variational matrix equations and the self-consistent-field principle for approximate molecular orbitals.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Supramolecular Chemistry
decks.description: Research design of interacting molecular assemblies.

includes: Host-guest recognition, cooperativity, self-assembly landscapes and stimuli-responsive molecular systems.

practice: Develop a quantitative assembly proposal with binding equations, competing hypotheses and validation measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive binding polynomials and distinguish affinity, avidity and cooperativity using competition data.
Propose responsive assemblies and specify controls separating reversible switching from degradation or aggregation.
Design self-assembling structures and predict equilibrium, kinetic trapping and defect consequences.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Statistical Learning
decks.description: Theory and inference for learning systems.

practice: Prove a learning bound and implement latent-variable and kernel methods on identifiable synthetic benchmarks.

outcomes.description: Construct positive-definite kernels, establish the representer principle and solve regularized kernel learning problems.
Derive EM and variational lower bounds and implement latent-variable inference with convergence diagnostics.
Derive representative concentration, uniform-convergence and capacity-dependent generalization bounds.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Natural-Language Processing

practice: Build a structured sequence system and compare it with a small neural baseline using linguistically targeted error sets.

outcomes.description: Construct token, morphological and contextual representations and assess their linguistic and multilingual limitations.
Evaluate language systems for task validity, factual error, ambiguity, bias and distribution shift.
Implement dynamic-programming parsing and sequence decoding and compare structured and neural language models.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Harmonic Analysis

includes: Fourier analysis in Lp spaces, convolution operators, approximate identities and tempered distributions.

practice: Prove Fourier-space estimates and solve generalized-transform problems where ordinary integrals fail.

outcomes.description: Establish convolution bounds and approximate-identity convergence and analyze representative multiplier operators.
Define tempered distributions and calculate distributional derivatives and Fourier transforms.
Prove Plancherel and representative Fourier convergence results in appropriate function spaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics

includes: Sufficiency, estimation and testing optimality, likelihood asymptotics and Bayesian decision theory.

practice: Derive competing estimators and tests and compare exact and asymptotic risk in specified models.

outcomes.description: Construct Bayes rules and compare admissibility, minimaxity and frequentist calibration.
Derive sufficient statistics, risk bounds and optimal estimators or tests in regular parametric models.
Derive consistency, asymptotic normality and likelihood-ratio approximations under explicit regularity conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical PDE Methods

includes: Finite differences, consistency/stability, finite elements, finite volumes and error verification.

practice: Implement heat, elliptic and conservation-law solvers with manufactured-solution and refinement studies.

outcomes.description: Implement finite-difference schemes and derive consistency, stability and representative convergence results.
Assemble finite-element weak forms and derive elementary energy-norm error estimates.
Implement conservative finite-volume fluxes and test shock resolution, conservation and grid convergence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Analysis

includes: Filtrations, martingales, stopping, Brownian motion, Ito integration and elementary stochastic differential equations.

practice: Prove stopped-process results and derive stochastic solution moments and boundary-hitting relations.

outcomes.description: Establish Brownian finite-dimensional and path properties and compare diffusion and jump-process behavior.
Construct square-integrable Ito integrals and apply Ito's formula to solve elementary stochastic differential equations.
Construct martingales and apply stopping and convergence theorems with integrability conditions checked.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Theory
